page.layout: One page of text in a single column; no margin notes. Running head at top with page number left and running title with chapter number right. Catchword-like hyphenated line "& or-" sits at the right below the last line, but is part of the text and is kept as a continuation line. Digitiser's watermark at bottom right is excluded.

main_text.p: ius loquitur, capite secundo secundæ Epistolæ ad Thessalonicenses, cujus mysterii natura semel intellecta à vobis probaretur, probata arriperetur ; denique arrepta vos moveret, imo permoveret, ad perducendum ejus utilitates ad effectum ; quarum utilitatum agmen ducit ruina Papalis imperii & unà totius Romanensis apparatûs missatici, Religionis & Ecclesiæ : opus quod, & unius periodi ambitu exscriberetis, & unius horæ spatio peragueretis : quam utilitatem longè plures excipiunt, quæ ex intelligentia mysterii iniquitatis, quam edimus, sunt redundaturæ in Ecclesias à Papismo reformatas ; imo in omnes Christianos. Nam cum penè ab ipsis incunabulis Ecclesiæ Christianæ, diversis, imo contrariis studiis decertatum fuerit, hinc ab ordine Ecclesiastico pro imperio, illinc à Magistratu pro libertate ; Papa inter hæc sibi imperium struente in Reges & nationes ; nec unquam orthodoxis & sanctis viris de ordine Ecclesiastico concordibus inter se, circa authoritatem Pastorum & Synodorum, & modum aut imperii, aut obsequii, qui Magistratui debetur circa sacra ; per nostram novam rationem, intellectam, probatam, & arreptam Papa ruet, & unà totum systema Romanense, Ecclesiæ, Religionis & missæ corruet : mutua erit συγκατάβασις Lutheranorum & Calvinistarum ; concident, ut exiguo pulveris jactu apum examina, privatæ stimulationes. & lites inter Pastores ejusdem sectæ & or-

page.notes: The line "ius loquitur..." is a fragment at the page start. Greek word "συγκατάβασις" is printed in italic and approximated; the reading of the accents is doubtful. Some words in the scan are blurred (e.g. "Romanensis", "Papalis") and may contain printing irregularities.
